title: REFERENCE temporal-acceptance bottleneck and owner handoff
source_bound_facts: execute_reference_interval constructs an independent full-step state and a two-half-step state from the same checkpoint and calls model%temporal_error(full_state, half_state)
transaction acceptance requires temporal_error <= transaction temporal_tolerance in addition to solver and hard mass gates
the admitted serialized REFERENCE backend binds temporal_error to fmr_serialized_temporal_identity

fmr_serialized_temporal_identity returns zero only when full-step and two-half-step pressure_head, water_content, ponding_depth and groundwater_level are exactly equal; otherwise it returns huge(real64)
therefore any finite temporal tolerance on this backend rejects a full/two-half state mismatch; tolerance magnitude cannot turn a mismatch into a graded temporal error
this exact full/two-half equality requirement does not logically require equality to the initial state, so accepted nonstationary execution is not declared impossible
F-PE04 observed no accepted nonstationary case and all accepted cases retained their own initial physical payload
